subject: PO delegation, ledger mapping and invoice trigger — proposed flow
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlaslabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlaslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO delegation + weekly invoice cadence proposal

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement had one practical request before we finalize the pilot: Atlas needs the PO to include a delegated approver field (PO_authority_id) that ties to our ERP so invoices can be auto-matched, and we prefer weekly invoice pulses for pilot consumption (rather than monthly).

A few specifics from our side:
- PO will be raised as a blanket commitment (PO# 12345) but invoices must reference a sub-PO token that maps to feature buckets (sku_buckets).
- Net terms: team prefers Net-45, but they will accept Net-30 if Redwood can provide a 1.5% early-payment discount applied when payment is made within 10 days.
- Attachments: I attached the PO stub Atlas will use for the pilot (Atlas_PO_12345.pdf).

Can Redwood accept: (1) PO_authority_id as a required field in the PO mapping, (2) weekly invoice pulses referencing the sub-PO tokens, and (3) the proposed early-pay discount if we land on Net-30?

Appreciate a quick confirmation so I can route to our AP team.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Director, Procurement — Atlas Labs

---

Maria —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to PO_authority_id mapping, yes to weekly invoice pulses, and we can evaluate the 1.5% early-pay discount with finance — need to confirm margins and ops for pilot scale.

Next steps from my side:
- Vanessa, can you confirm the invoice generation pipeline can include a sub-PO token field and produce weekly batches?
- Ben, can you run a quick estimate on unit economics if we offer 1.5% EPD for Net-30 on the expected pilot volume (approx $35k ARR monthly consumption)?

Maria — I attached our standard PO template (redwood_PO_template.pdf) to show field names we can already populate; Vanessa and Ben will confirm controls.

Best,
Sergio
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PO delegation + weekly invoice cadence proposal

Sergio / Maria —

Confirming from ops: we already support a free-form PO metadata field and can add PO_authority_id to our mapping table. Weekly invoice pulses are supported but there are two operational notes:

1) Sub-PO token mapping: we require the token to be present on invoice lines (max length 40 chars). We'll mirror it to the ledger reference field so Atlas' ERP can auto-match.
2) Timing: weekly pulses will be generated on Mondays; invoices pushed to SFTP / EDIFACT by 11:00 PT. If Atlas wants a different cutoff we can accommodate with a week-of-month override.

I will add PO_authority_id and sub-po-token to the redwood_PO_template.pdf and send the revised template in a separate email.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Billing Ops — Redwood Inference

On Mon, 6 Sep 2026 at 13:15 -07:00, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlaslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO delegation + weekly invoice cadence proposal

Team —

Quick economics note: at the pilot consumption you outlined (~$35k monthly), a 1.5% early-pay discount reduces our invoice by $525/month. On a 3-month pilot that's ~$1.6k impact; acceptable if no additional credit is extended and the contract remains non-recurring for pilot. If Atlas is moving to a committed annual bucket post-pilot we can bake a volume-tiered discount that offsets this early-pay concession.

Options for Maria to consider:
- Option A (preferred): Redwood accepts Net-30 + 1.5% EPD during pilot; Atlas routes weekly pulses as proposed.
- Option B: Keep Net-45, no EPD, Redwood issues weekly pulses but invoices on a 30-day terms internally (we'd still collect on our normal Net-45 cadence). Not ideal for Atlas' AP automation.

If Atlas is okay with Option A, I'll draft a short amendment with the EPD clause and attach it to the pilot SOW.

Ben Carter
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics — Redwood Inference
